subject: SIG clarification — 'Privileged backup key' interpretation and evidence options
messages:
From: Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@fintrust.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: security_ops@fintrust.com
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG Q6 — clarification requested on 'privileged backup key' wording

Tessa — thanks for working with us on the SIG. One of our reviewers flagged SIG question Q6 (backups / key ownership) as ambiguous for our regulator review. The text reads: "Does the vendor maintain separate backup keys for privileged access?"

Two possible readings from our side: 1) Are backups encrypted with a key that is distinct from the production data encryption key? 2) Does the vendor maintain a separate privileged key used by operators for backup restore operations?

Our regulator would like a written interpretation and artifacts that demonstrate how keys are segregated and where they are stored (HSM vs KMS vs software). Specifically: algorithmic separation (different CMKs), storage boundary (HSM custody), and rotation evidence. Can you clarify which interpretation Redwood intends to provide as the SIG answer and what artifacts you can supply? If easier, we can do a 30-minute call next week.

Thanks,
Angela Ruiz
Sr. Information Security Manager
FinTrust Bank
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@fintrust.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG Q6 — clarification requested on 'privileged backup key' wording

Hi Angela — thanks, good catch. We see the same two plausible readings. To avoid regulator friction, we propose to adopt and document Interpretation A as our SIG response and provide artifacts that explicitly cover both aspects:

Interpretations (we will mark one in the SIG answer):
A) Backups are encrypted with a separate Customer Master Key (CMK) distinct from the live production data CMK; backup key material is HSM-backed. This shows cryptographic separation and HSM custody.
B) There exists an operator-privileged key for restore operations (used for orchestration/restore flows) — we will state whether that key is a separate CMK or an alias-based management pattern.

Suggested artifacts we can provide:
- KMS key alias to CMK mapping (redacted)
- Key policy excerpt showing HSM-backed provision and allowed principals
- Key creation and rotation timestamps (sample CSV)
- HSM vendor attestation template (pdf)
- Diagram showing where backups are encrypted and where keys are stored
- SOC 2 control mapping that references key management controls

I've attached a draft SIG response (SIG_Q6-draft-response.md) and a sample rotation export (kms-rotation-sample.csv). If that looks reasonable, we can schedule a 30-min call to confirm wording with your team and then finalize artifacts.

Proposed times: Tue 02/24 10:00–10:30 PST or Wed 02/25 13:00–13:30 PST.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@fintrust.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Feb 2026 12:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG Q6 — clarification requested on 'privileged backup key' wording

Thanks Tessa — that scope makes sense. Two follow-ups before the call: 1) our regulator will want explicit confirmation that backup key material is HSM-protected (not just KMS software-based keys). Can you confirm you can provide attestation or vendor paperwork? 2) For rotation evidence, a CSV with key ids and rotation timestamps is fine, but it must show that the backup CMK was rotated independently of the production CMK.

Please include our PV team on the call: security_ops@fintrust.com. Tue 02/24 10:00 PST works for us.

Angela
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@fintrust.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Feb 2026 09:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG Q6 — clarification requested on 'privileged backup key' wording

Looping in a bit of detail from the engineering side — we can absolutely provide artifacts that satisfy Interpretation A and show separation. Practical artifacts we will prepare: 
- KMS alias -> CMK mapping (image: kps-mapping.png)
- Sample rotation log: key_id, created_at, last_rotated_at (kms-rotation-sample.csv)
- Key policy excerpt (redacted) showing HSM-backed enforcement for the CMK used for backups
- HSM attestation template (hsm-attestation-sample.pdf) — we will coordinate with our HSM provider for a signed copy if the customer requires it
- Redacted audit trail showing an operator restore flow (redacted event ids)

Action items (high level):
- Marissa: produce mapping image, rotation CSV, key policy excerpt (ETA 2026-02-28)
- Tessa: draft SIG text that picks Interpretation A and references artifacts (ETA 2026-03-01)
- Neha: compliance review of the drafted SIG answer and artifacts (ETA 2026-03-02)

I've attached two samples to this thread for review: hsm-attestation-sample.pdf and kps-mapping.png. We'll keep any PII redacted.

Marissa
Director, Security Engineering
Redwood Inference
From: security_ops@fintrust.com
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 22 Feb 2026 14:00:00 -0800
Subject: Re: SIG Q6 scheduling — PV team joining

Tessa/Marissa — confirmed. PV team (security_ops@fintrust.com) will join the Tue 02/24 10:00 PST slot. Agenda: 1) Confirm Redwood's chosen interpretation for SIG Q6; 2) Walk through the artifacts you will provide and acceptability for regulator; 3) Next steps and delivery dates.

Also, please be prepared to call out whether the backup CMK uses a separate key-derivation mechanism or merely a key alias. Our regulator treats those differently.

– FinTrust PV Team
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Angela Ruiz <angela.ruiz@fintrust.com>, security_ops@fintrust.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Feb 2026 10:33:00 -0800
Subject: Post-call: agreed interpretation and evidence plan for SIG Q6

Thanks everyone for the call this morning — summary and confirmed actions below.

Agreed interpretation for SIG Q6: Redwood will answer per Interpretation A —: backups are encrypted with a CMK that is distinct from the production data CMK; the backup CMK is HSM-backed (hardware-backed key material) and rotated on a defined schedule. The customer clarified that an alias-only separation is insufficient; they require proof the underlying key material is distinct and HSM-protected.

Artifacts to provide (final list):
- KMS alias -> CMK mapping image (kps-mapping.png) — Marissa
- Rotation export csv showing independent rotation entries for backup CMK and production CMK (kms-rotation-sample.csv) — Marissa
- Key policy excerpt with HSM enforcement clause (redacted) — Marissa
- HSM vendor attestation (signed pdf) or vendor-signed stamping (hsm-attestation-sample.pdf placeholder until signed) — Marissa
- One-page SIG answer text we will submit (SIG_Q6-draft-response.md) — Tessa
- Redacted restore audit trail (redacted ids included) — Marissa
- Link to meeting recording and the shared Drive folder (meeting-recording-link.txt) — Tessa

Timelines: Marissa -> artifacts delivered by 2026-02-28 end of day. Tessa -> populate SIG Q6 and submit draft to Neha by 2026-03-01. Neha -> final sign-off by 2026-03-02.

Open items:
- Marissa to confirm whether HSM vendor will provide a signed attestation or we provide a vendor contact+template; update in reply.
- Tessa/Neha to ensure the drafted SIG answer includes explicit language on algorithmic separation and references the attestation/rotation CSV.

Attachments referenced above are available in the shared folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1A2bSIGQ6-evidence

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
